findings.title: isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is False for spawn-context processes, so hung flushers are never killed
findings.body: Processes are created with `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which is `SpawnProcess`. `SpawnProcess` subclasses `BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.context.Process`, which is what `multiprocessing.Process` refers to. So `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is always False for real flusher processes. The original code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally; this PR guards it with that isinstance check, so `kill()` is now dead code. When a flusher is detected as hung, the old process keeps running while `_create_process_for_shards` starts a replacement on the same shards. The result is duplicate flushers on one shard (possible duplicate segments to Kafka), leaked processes, and eventually the MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS crash. The same check in `join()` (around line 346) means `terminate()` is never called either. Check against `multiprocessing.context.BaseProcess`, or use `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`.

findings.title: Added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched
findings.body: `test_basic` begins with `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`. The new `time.sleep(0.1)` ("Give flusher threads time to process after drift change") calls the patched function and does nothing. The test therefore still races: `step.join()` sets `stopped` immediately after the drift change, and the flusher thread may exit before flushing, making `(msg,) = messages` flaky. The extra `step.poll()` doesn't help either. Capture the real sleep before patching, or poll/wait until `messages` is non-empty with a timeout.

findings.title: join() can break out of the loop and skip waiting for or terminating the remaining processes
findings.body: In the new per-process join loop, once the deadline expires the code does `break`. This skips the wait and the `terminate()` for all remaining processes. The original code always attempted `terminate()` after the wait. With multiple processes, one slow process can consume the whole timeout and leave the others neither awaited nor terminated. They are only cleaned up if they are daemons and the parent exits. Iterate over all processes and terminate stragglers after the deadline instead of breaking.

findings.title: Docstring claims one process per shard, but the number of processes is capped by max_processes
findings.body: The class docstring says "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing." Actually `num_processes = min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards))` and shards are distributed round-robin, so processes can serve several shards. The CLI option `--flusher-processes` defaults to 1, so by default a single process handles all shards. The docstring misleads readers and operators about the default behavior.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag keys (`shard` vs `shards`) and comma-joined shard lists as tag values
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `segment_size_bytes` are tagged with `shard`, but `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses `shards`. Dashboards and queries that group on one key will silently miss the other. The tag value is also a comma-joined list of shards (e.g. `0,4,8`), which changes with the process/shard mapping and creates new tag values on every assignment change. `flusher_unhealthy` uses a single-shard `shard` tag, so the same key now has different value formats across metrics.

findings.title: submit() now makes per-process Redis calls on every message, with redundant memory-info queries
findings.body: Before, `submit` called `record_stored_segments()` and `get_memory_info()` once on one buffer. Now it iterates all per-process buffers. Each buffer is built over a subset of shards but points at the same Redis cluster(s), so cluster-wide `get_memory_info()` is repeated N times and the results summed. The used/available ratio is unchanged, but Redis INFO round-trips on the consumer's main thread scale with the flusher process count, which defeats the goal of keeping the main thread minimal. Query memory once (e.g. via the main buffer) instead.

findings.title: Unused `_create_process_for_shard` helper
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard)` is never called. `_ensure_processes_alive` calls `_create_process_for_shards` directly. This is dead code and should be removed.

findings.title: No validation of --flusher-processes; negative values crash SpanFlusher
findings.body: `--flusher-processes` is a plain `int` with no lower bound. `0` silently falls back to one process per shard because of `max_processes or len(shards)`. A negative value makes `num_processes` negative, so `process_to_shards_map` is empty. The distribution loop then does `i % self.num_processes`, which is 0 for `-1` and raises `KeyError` on the empty map. Use `click.IntRange(min=1)`.

findings.title: New test only checks process counts, not distribution, flush behavior or restart logic
findings.body: `test_flusher_processes_limit` asserts `len(processes)==2` and that the total shard count is 4. It does not check that each shard appears in exactly one process or that spans from different shards are flushed. It also doesn't exercise `_ensure_processes_alive` (restart/kill) or the real spawn path, since it uses the threaded `produce_to_pipe` mode. The restart/kill regression (spawn `Process` not matching the `isinstance` check) therefore goes untested.
